title: Lee Young's name Leonidas and how his father chose it
summary: Willard asks about his full name; he explains it was given by his schoolteacher father, who liked Greek history, and that he went by Lee from high school.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: MS .WILLARD: November 8, 1977. The Oral History, with Lee Young.
Lee, I see in two biographies on you, in the Chilton and Feather books, that your full name is -- well, you pronounce it.
Leonidas. Leonidis. It's a Greek pronunciation, isn't it?
Yes, it is. Leonidas Leonidis Raymond Young, Senior. I also gave that name to someone else.
You mean you haven't enjoyed that name?

Well, I haven't used that name. The only time that name was ever really used was when I was in Junior High School. All the teachers called me Leonidas Leonidis. But when I got to high school, it was Lee, because, you know, it'd kind of a difficult name, and they pronounced it Leonetis, Leonatis, anything but Leonidis Leonidas ... so ...
Well, how did your parents happen to name you Leonidas Leonidas?
Well, my father was a schoolteacher --

he was a professor of music, and he also taught history at the University of New Orleans, and he was in to Greek, I guess, and you know, I read about Leonidas incidentally. You know, Leonidas was a great warrior or something; he held the bridge with a thousand men, he held 10,000 soldiers -- and when you, you know, when you're very young, that's kind of interesting, because you can just imagine the warriors fighting and this guy holding all these people at bay, for three days, I think it was!
So at that time, I guess I was kind of proud of Leonidas. Probably got beat up an awful lot, because of that.
Yeah, I guess you could say that.
